title: Retrocausal Canon Formation and the Political Economy of the Past How Semantic Rent is Extracted from Retroactively Constructed History
creator: Lee Sharks
description:
A working theoretical essay by Lee Sharks extending retrocausal canon formation into a political economy of historical visibility.

The paper does not propose supernatural backward causation. It argues that later acts of interpretation, indexing, tagging, citation, ranking, and retrieval reorganize which earlier works become visible, valuable, related, and canonical. In machine-mediated systems, that retroactive reorganization becomes executable infrastructure rather than literary interpretation alone. The essay introduces semantic rent on inherited cultural material, canon-making infrastructure, personalized pasts, canonical crystallization, and prospective provenance anchors described as “semantic futures contracts.” These are theoretical models and analogies, not financial instruments or demonstrated causal laws.
